title: Burrowing Owl with moth
subtitle: A burrowing owl in low flight at Rocky Mountain Arsenal, Colorado, locked onto a moth in mid-air. Soft, uniform grass behind the bird sits alongside finely-detailed feather and face structure — giving noise-reduction tools both a smooth gradient region and a high-detail region to handle.

critique.text: This original RAW image serves as the baseline, exhibiting a high level of luminance noise (grain) across the background that softens the overall image and obscures fine feather details on the owl. The underlying sharpness is decent but muddy due to the noise. The edited versions all attempt to smooth the background and enhance subject detail using various AI tools. Overall, DxO (Image 4) performed the best with incredible sharpness and clean backgrounds, followed closely by Lightroom (Image 5) for a natural look. Topaz (Image 1) was highly detailed but slightly artificial, while ON1 (Image 3) ranked last due to severe background artifacts. The noisy original RAW is arguably preferable to the highly artifacted ON1 edit.

images.title: DxO PureRAW 6
images.caption: DxO using DxO DeepPrime wD3 with Lens Sharpness Optimization increased to 150 (Strong)

critique.text: DxO DeepPrime XD3 offers arguably the best balance of noise reduction and sharpness in the set. The background is rendered buttery smooth, completely eliminating the heavy noise of the RAW without introducing the painterly artifacts seen in ON1. The strong lens sharpness optimization has pulled an incredible amount of fine detail out of the owl's feathers and the flying insect, making it noticeably crisper than the Lightroom version while avoiding the slightly over-processed look of the Topaz edit.

images.title: Lightroom Denoise
images.caption: Lightroom AI Denoise at default settings

critique.text: Lightroom's AI Denoise provides a highly natural and pleasing result. It handles the background noise exceptionally well, clearing up the RAW's heavy grain and creating a smooth backdrop that rivals DxO. In terms of sharpness, it retains excellent natural detail in the owl's feathers compared to the muddy RAW, though it is softer and less aggressively sharpened than the Topaz or DxO versions. This makes it a great choice for a highly realistic, cleanly processed look without the risk of over-sharpening.

images.title: Topaz Photo
images.caption: Topaz Photo with noise reduction and subject sharpening using default values

critique.text: The Topaz AI edit successfully removes the heavy grain seen in the original RAW, producing a much cleaner background. However, the default subject sharpening is quite aggressive. While the owl's face and wing feathers are exceptionally crisp, they border on looking slightly over-sharpened or 'crunchy' compared to the more natural Lightroom edit. It ranks highly for detail extraction but loses a little ground on natural rendering compared to DxO.

images.title: ON1 RAW
images.caption: ON1 RAW with NoNoise and TackSharp

critique.text: The ON1 NoNoise and TackSharp processing yielded the weakest results of the edited batch. While it managed to sharpen the owl and reduce standard grain compared to the RAW, it introduced severe, unnatural 'wormy' and painterly artifacts throughout the out-of-focus background. This glassy, smeared texture is highly distracting and makes the overall image look heavily processed and artificial compared to the smoother, much more successful noise reduction from Lightroom and DxO.
